cosy-lesson.title: The Future of Fusion Energy: Clean power for everyone?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Fusion – the process of joining two or more things together to form a single entity.

p.em: Example: Nuclear fusion powers the sun and other stars.

cosy-blockquote.p: Fission – the action of dividing or splitting something into two or more parts.

p.em: Example: Traditional nuclear power plants use fission to generate electricity.

cosy-blockquote.p: Plasma – an ionized gas consisting of positive ions and free electrons.

p.em: Example: In a fusion reactor, the fuel must be heated until it becomes plasma.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sustainability – the ability to be maintained at a certain rate or level.

p.em: Example: Fusion is seen as a key to long-term energy sustainability.

cosy-blockquote.p: Breakthrough – a sudden, dramatic, and important discovery or development.

p.em: Example: Scientists recently achieved a major breakthrough in net energy gain.

cosy-blockquote.p: Isotopes – forms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.

p.em: Example: Deuterium and tritium are isotopes of hydrogen used in fusion.

cosy-blockquote.p: Magnetic confinement – using magnetic fields to contain fusion fuel in the form of a plasma.

p.em: Example: The tokamak design uses magnetic confinement to stabilize the reaction.

cosy-blockquote.p: Net energy gain – when the energy generated is greater than the energy required to start the reaction.

p.em: Example: Achieving net energy gain is the primary goal of commercial fusion research.

cosy-blockquote.p: Abundance – a very large quantity of something.

p.em: Example: Hydrogen is found in great abundance in the Earth's oceans.

cosy-blockquote.p: Radioactive waste – hazardous waste that contains radioactive material.

p.em: Example: One advantage of fusion is that it produces very little long-lived radioactive waste.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, how does nuclear fusion achieve power generation without using highly dangerous heavy elements?
★ When commercial fusion is achieved, how will energy grids be transformed?

Based on the study, what distinguishes traditional nuclear fission from controlled stellar fusion?
★ What is your personal opinion on traditional nuclear fission power?

According to the paper, what extreme thermal barriers must scientists overcome to stabilize superheated plasma?
★ What is the most promising renewable energy source in your local area?

What data presented in the article suggests that fusion could guarantee global energy sustainability for millions of years?
★ How often do you think about resource depletion and sustainability?

According to researchers, what recent laboratory breakthrough brought us closer to ignition?
★ Do you trust science to deliver completely clean unlimited energy in your lifetime?

Based on the text, why are deuterium and tritium preferred isotopes for laser-ignition systems?
★ If you could invest in any scientific startup, would it be energy or space travel?

What unique parameters define a tokamak's magnetic confinement configuration?
★ Are you willing to pay slightly higher bills if it guarantees clean, green energy?

What empirical evidence in the report supports the claims of achieving a true net energy gain?
★ Do you remember any power outages from your childhood? How did you manage?

According to the study, how does the global abundance of hydrogen isotopes solve geopolitical resource competition?
★ Have you ever visited a power plant or major industrial facility?

What data presented in the paper supports the assertion that fusion leaves zero long-lived radioactive waste?
★ Do you think nuclear energy will always face negative public bias regardless of safety?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this hypothesis, commercial fusion plants will completely replace fossil fuel grids by 2060.
★ Would you live near a safe, operational nuclear fusion power plant?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, traditional nuclear fission facilities will be phased out to protect public health.
★ Do you think humans will eventually build cities powered completely by artificial stars?

Imagine future research proves that superheated plasma can be sustained indefinitely inside micro-reactors, how would transportation systems change?
★ Should solar panels and wind turbines be mandatory on all new residential buildings?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, global energy sustainability indexes will reach 100% across all continents.
★ Do you think energy abundance would end global wars and territorial conflicts?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, a portable reactor breakthrough will enable deep space travel within the next century.
★ Would you support a ban on gas-powered cars within the next ten years?

Imagine future research shows that harvesting ocean isotopes causes no marine damage, how would scientists expand fuel extraction?
★ Do you think rich nations should fund clean energy setups for developing countries?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, advanced magnetic confinement fields will make solar and wind storage completely obsolete.
★ Would you trust a community energy grid run entirely by autonomous AI algorithms?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, achieving a stable net energy gain of Q=50 will make electrical power virtually free.
★ How has your personal lifestyle changed to reduce your environmental impact?

Imagine future research proves that an abundance of deuterium-tritium reactions causes minor ozone heat traps, would scientists have to limit energy production?
★ Do you think nuclear energy will always face negative public bias regardless of safety?

If future research continues to support this hypothesis, we will completely eliminate the issue of radioactive waste in the power sector.
★ What is the most exciting scientific development you are currently following?

ul.li: Incorrect: The government should invest more → Correct: Governments should invest more ((Generalizing with plurals))
Incorrect: I am looking forward to see it → Correct: I am looking forward to seeing it ((Looking forward to + -ing))
Incorrect: It didn't happened yet → Correct: It hasn't happened yet ((Present Perfect for 'yet'))
Incorrect: Explain me the process → Correct: Explain the process to me ((Direct/Indirect object))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
